new_statements.rule_in_words: In Collins's own field transcription of his Bobot (Werinama) 200-item wordlist, stress is taken to fall on the penultimate syllable by default; deviations are marked with an acute. In the Bobot column only two forms are so marked, both with final stress: bakatáu 'plant' (no. 84, p. 143) and vitól 'thick' (no. 157, p. 145). All other Bobot forms are unmarked, i.e. penultimate.
new_statements.exceptions: Two Bobot forms marked final-stressed: bakatáu 'plant', vitól 'thick'. (Note 28 on final stress in metmeten refers to Banda, not Bobot.)
new_statements.domain_note: Transcription convention for isolated citation forms in a comparative wordlist; applies jointly to six East Seram languages, not a Bobot-specific phonological description. No statement about phrase-level accent or suffixed words.
new_statements.identity_note: The quoted statement covers Collins's Bobot wordlist from Werinama village (the coastal Bobot dialect; (N) Naiyaba and (T) Tobo variants also cited in the list). Glottolog bobo1254 = ISO bty, dialects Werinama/Hatumeten/Atiahu/Ahtiago/Ntau. Caution for anyone using ABVD: ABVD list 16 labelled 'Bobot' (bobo1254) actually contains the Masiwang (bnf, Kota Baru) column of Collins 1986; ABVD list 278 'Werinama' is the real Bobot data.

sources.locator: p. 141, Appendix: A comparative wordlist of the languages of Eastern Seram, notational preamble (Bobot list = Werinama); marked exceptions in the Bobot column at p. 143 no. 84 and p. 145 no. 157
sources.note: Appendix header p.141: 'With regard to the phonetic notation, stress is penultimate unless otherwise marked.' — a transcription convention covering all six wordlists incl. Bobot (Werinama). In the Bobot column only two of ~200 forms carry a stress mark, both final: no. 84 bakatáu 'plant' (p.143) and no. 157 vitól 'thick' (p.145). Note 28 (final stress on metmeten, p.138) concerns Banda, not Bobot. No other statement on Bobot stress.

sources.note: Stress discussed only for Asilulu vs Hoamoal languages ('Stress in Hoamoal languages is always penultimate...'); Bobot appears only as 'Hatumeten' in Stresemann's classification and in a village table (Tunsa = Bobot). Nothing on Bobot stress.

sources.citation: ABVD (Austronesian Basic Vocabulary Database) lists 16 'Bobot' (J. Collins) and 278 'Werinama' (J. Collins)
sources.note: Wordlists only. List 16 labelled 'Bobot' actually reproduces the MASIWANG (Kota Baru) column of Collins 1986 (hasan, kabalit, lalait, uha, ahás...); list 278 'Werinama' is the real Bobot column (-niman, avet, kamuin, ko...). Sporadic acute marks copied from Collins; no stress statement.
